newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon detains second opposition unionist.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon detains second opposition unionist.

text.p: A Beirut prosecutor ordered on Wednesday the detention of a second labour leader, Yasser Nehme, for interrogation on charges carrying at least six months in jail.

Prosecutor Abdallah Bitar issued a similar order against leftist labour leader Elias Abou Rizk, charged last week with impersonating the head of the General Labour Confederation (CGTL) and usurping office by force.
Abou Rizk remains in custody after investigative judge Saeed Mirza refused to release him on bail, judicial sources said.

Nehme, secretary general of Abou Rizk's branch of the CGTL, and Abou Rizk are suspected of having "publicized false or exaggerated news outside Lebanon in a manner that undermined Lebanon's reputation or its financial status", a source said.

Investigations in last week's lawsuit revealed that Abou Rizk and Nehme had sent letters to the International Labour Confederation claiming that Abou Rizk had received threats of assassination, the sources said.
The letters were sent after controversial CGTL elections last month split the confederation and resulted in the election of two leaderships headed by Abou Rizk and Ghneim al-Zoghbi.

If convicted of the initial charges filed by al-Zoghbi, Abou Rizk would face at least seven years in prison. If convicted of the latest charges filed by the state's prosecutor, both men would be fined and jailed for at least least six months.
The arrest of Abou Rizk has brought widespread protests from political parties, labour unions and opposition politicians.

Abou Rizk's leadership repeatedly called for pay rises, strikes and demonstrations and accused the government of ignoring the plight of the poor. In February 1996 the army imposed a curfew on much of the country to stop demonstrations called by Abou Rizk during a general strike.
